info.title: Biohub Officiel V6
info.description:
# Biohub Cell Tracking — 3D+Time Cell Detection & Lineage Reconstruction

## Overview
A CPU-optimized pipeline for detecting and tracking zebrafish embryo cells 
across 3D+time fluorescence microscopy volumes, including division (mitosis) 
event detection for full lineage reconstruction.

## Pipeline Architecture

**1. Detection** — Per-frame cell centroid detection via anisotropy-aware 
Gaussian smoothing + local maxima extraction, with percentile-based 
normalization for noise robustness.

**2. Linking** — Frame-to-frame association using the Hungarian algorithm 
(Linear Assignment Problem) on physically-scaled Euclidean distances 
(z=1.625µm, y=x=0.40625µm/voxel).

**3. Gap Closing** — Recovers tracks interrupted by a single missed 
detection by searching two frames ahead.

**4. Division Detection** — Identifies mitosis events via geometric 
constraints: daughter cell symmetry, inter-daughter distance, and 
trajectory angle divergence.

## Key Engineering Decisions
- Zarr v3 array accessed at canonical path `0/`, shape `(T, Z, Y, X)`
- Single-chunk-per-timepoint reads avoid loading full volumes into memory
- All thresholds tuned for CPU-only execution within Kaggle's 12h limit

## Version Log
- v6: Aligned with official data spec (zarr v3, path `0/`); fixed gap-closing 
  indexing bug; added trajectory-angle filter to reduce false-positive divisions
